iterations.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Create one production-quality desktop game UI concept for the PvE auto-battler "Trials of Gipath" in Cursed Lands / Evil Islands. This is an implementable screenshot mockup, not a poster. Landscape 16:10, crisp readable interface at 1280×800.
Input images: 1 is the CURRENT ACTUAL playable mode: retain its early-2000s low-poly boar, goblin, toad, wolf, bat, mossy ruined courtyard, native textures and camera language, but REMOVE its overloaded interface. 2 is the actual original game's interface/material/style reference: restrained tarnished bronze, dark translucent backing, warm ivory serif titles, original game atmosphere. 3 is ONLY the Auto Chess composition reference, especially an unobstructed field and unboxed miniature recruits and reserves. Do not copy Dota characters, branding, purple magic, stone tile grids or its multiplayer ranking.
Primary request: Much cleaner, beautiful, highly usable game HUD, grounded in the actual Evil Islands game, with extremely little permanent chrome. The battlefield dominates 78 percent of the image. Keep actual terrain/units visually close to image1, no upgrades to the scene's graphics style. Isometric-ish overhead camera, original mossy grey-brown stone ruins, grass and native original figures. Show one red-bar boar far side, three tiny original units friendly side with blue health bars. Clear center, no panels in the center or at the sides.
Layout: Thin open recruitment shelf across the upper-left 75%: exactly five original model previews (boar, sling goblin, toad, grey wolf, small red bat), 3 coin price beneath each, subtle 1/3 duplicate progress only under boar. No rectangular cards. Small refresh icon and '2'. Narrow weathered bronze shelf line may gently ground the models, no thick slab. Top right a compact two-line round readout with text 'WAVE 1 / 18' and 'Preparing', plus small menu icon. No game title/header bar. Along lower edge, six reserve places: one actual boar miniature then five faint short marks, no boxes. 'Army 3 / 3' small at lower left. Lower right only coin icon '6', three small life icons, and a single modest dark bronze button labeled 'Start battle'. Button looks from original game, not bright flat yellow.
Typography: few short labels, excellent hierarchy and contrast, warm ivory. No long creature labels always visible, no repeated labels or instructions. Creature names and stats are hover/selection only, not shown in this image. Wide breathing room.
Avoid: progress strip, opponent panel, sidebar, tutorial box, full-width top/bottom opaque panels, decorative filigree, logos, title, watermark, grid overlay, blue deployment rectangle, rings under every unit, modern dashboard, neon, big empty card slots. The intended screenshot is the neutral PREPARATION state with no selection. UI should feel like carefully restored Evil Islands craft, extremely restrained, with no invented abilities or mechanics.

iterations.assessment: Subjective visual target rating: open battlefield, coherent muted bronze, concise readable controls. Generated concept is not proof of runtime usability.
iterations.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Refine this exact Cursed Lands / Evil Islands PvE auto-battler UI screenshot into a highly polished, genuinely implementable design. Keep the composition, actual original-game low-poly creatures, native rough stone/grass environment, camera, completely open battlefield, and all positions. Do NOT beautify or redraw the game world into modern graphics. Change only these UI details:
1. The three glossy candy-red hearts are wrong for the original game's art. Replace with ONE small understated tarnished-bronze outlined heart icon and warm ivory text '3/3'. Keep the coin and '6'. Keep resources aligned on one compact baseline at bottom right.
2. Reduce 'Start battle' button size about 20%, leaving a 16px right and bottom inset. Use a very thin worn bronze edge, dark charcoal-brown center, warm ivory serif text at a readable but moderate size. No decorative spikes/filigree. It is the only primary action.
3. Keep top-right round readout compact with 16px inset from top/right edges and proper padding. Text exactly 'Wave 1 / 18' and 'Preparing'. Small discreet adjacent menu icon. Tone down the heavy frame: only a thin weathered bronze rim, matching the actual game's framed UI.
4. On the first recruit, put '1/3' alongside its coin '3' on the same baseline, separated by a little space; remove the detached below-shelf counter. Other four offers retain only coin '3'. Keep the single thin shelf line behind the models. No card rectangles. Add a very tiny lock icon at the upper-right of each offer as a quiet hover affordance, not a row of labels.
5. Consistent warm ivory readable typography, original-game serif for round / main action, simple legible small numerals. Use the same bronze material language in all three interface groups. Ensure fine contrast, generous spacing, no overlaps.
Preserve: one enemy on far side, three friendly units, original-style health bars, five model offers, exactly six reserve places of which one is occupied, 'Army 3 / 3'. NO new information, labels, panels, bars, game title, sidebar, tutorial, character circles, combat grid, glow, watermark, fake attributes. The result should be a quiet finished native game interface with almost all attention on the battlefield. Landscape 16:10.
